mcQuestions.q: When text is moved at the beginning of a paragraph by five spaces to the right it is called
optionExplanations: A right indent moves the entire right edge of a paragraph away from the right margin — it affects every line, not just the first.
A mirror indent is used in documents with facing pages, where left and right margins are swapped on alternating pages. It doesn't describe moving the first line.
A hanging indent is the opposite of a first-line indent — the first line stays at the margin while all subsequent lines are indented to the right.
✓ Correct. A first-line indent moves only the very first line of a paragraph to the right, which is the standard paragraph indent used in essays and books.

mcQuestions.q: What does PDF stand for?
optionExplanations: Portable Data File is not a real format. PDF was never designed solely for data — it preserves the visual layout of documents.
Printer Description File does not exist as a standard format. PDFs are designed to be read across devices, not just printed.
Page Description Format is close but incorrect. PostScript is a page description language, but PDF stands for something different.
✓ Correct. PDF stands for Portable Document Format — developed by Adobe to preserve formatting (fonts, images, layout) consistently across different operating systems and software.

mcQuestions.q: What is pagination used for?
options: Setting the colour of the text used on pages
optionExplanations: Pagination does not remove pages. Removing content is an editing function — pagination only controls how content is divided.
Aligning pages refers to layout/margins, not pagination. Pagination controls the flow and numbering of pages, not their alignment.
✓ Correct. Pagination divides a document or digital content into separate, numbered pages, controlling where page breaks occur and how content flows from one page to the next.
Text colour is a typography/formatting setting, completely unrelated to pagination.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following affects file size?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Colour depth (bit depth) determines how many colours each pixel can represent. A higher bit depth means more data stored per pixel, directly increasing the file size of an image.
Hard-disk space is where files are stored, but it doesn't determine the size of the file itself. A file's size is fixed regardless of available storage.
Processor speed affects how quickly a file can be opened or processed, but has no effect on how much data the file contains.
Screen size affects how a file is displayed, but the file's data content — and therefore its size — is independent of the display device.

mcQuestions.q: What is the primary function of a clapper board?
options: To indicate the beginning of a shot
To show which scenes belong together
To synchronise video and audio images
To show colour samples for copying film
optionExplanations: While a clapperboard is used at the start of a shot, 'indicating the beginning' is a secondary function. Its primary technical purpose is synchronisation, not just signalling the start.
Scene organisation is handled by the script supervisor and shot lists, not by the clapperboard itself.

✓ Correct. The sharp 'clap' creates a visible spike in the audio waveform. Editors align this spike with the frame where the board closes, perfectly synchronising separately recorded video and audio tracks in post-production.
Colour charts/colour cards are separate tools used for colour calibration. A clapperboard does not contain colour samples.

mcQuestions.q: What does authoring software allow a user to do?
optionExplanations: Watching media is a function of media players (e.g., VLC, Windows Media Player), not authoring software. Authoring is about creating, not consuming.

✓ Correct. Authoring software (e.g., Adobe Animate, Articulate) allows users to create and combine multimedia elements — text, images, audio, video, interactivity — into a complete, publishable multimedia product.
Copying content is a file management or ripping function. Authoring software is used to create original multimedia products, not to duplicate existing ones.
Separating text from graphics describes OCR or image editing operations. Authoring software integrates elements together rather than separating them.

mcQuestions.q: What is required to use copyrighted images on your webpage?
options: The owner's permission to use material
Nothing more as copyrighted material is free to use
optionExplanations: A software licence governs the use of software applications, not the content created or owned by someone else. You need a content licence or permission, not a software licence.
Adding a disclaimer does not grant legal permission to use copyrighted material. Copyright law protects creators regardless of whether you acknowledge their ownership.

✓ Correct. Copyright is automatically assigned to creators. To legally use their images, you must obtain explicit permission — typically through a written licence or agreement. Failing to do so is copyright infringement.
This is completely incorrect. Copyrighted material is not free to use — the copyright holder has exclusive rights to reproduce, distribute and display their work.

mcQuestions.q: Tweening is the process of generating
optionExplanations: Hand-drawn animation describes traditional cel animation, where every frame is drawn by hand. Tweening is the computer-automated alternative that eliminates this work.

✓ Correct. Tweening (in-betweening) automatically generates the intermediate frames between two keyframes, creating smooth transitions of position, scale, rotation or shape as defined by the animator.
Keyframes are created by the animator to define the start and end states of a movement. Tweening generates the frames in between keyframes — it does not create the keyframes themselves.
Jerky images would result from too few frames or dropped frames — the opposite of what tweening achieves. Tweening creates smooth, fluid motion.

mcQuestions.q: Anti-aliasing is used when
options: There are too many pixels on the screen
A low-resolution image is used at a higher resolution
A high-resolution image is used at a lower resolution
optionExplanations: Poor game performance relates to frame rate and hardware optimisation, not anti-aliasing. While anti-aliasing can reduce performance slightly, it's not used to fix slow frame rates.
Too many pixels would result in a sharp, detailed image — not a jagged one. Anti-aliasing addresses jaggedness on diagonal edges, not pixel density.
Using a low-resolution image at higher resolution causes blurriness or pixelation, but anti-aliasing is not the solution for this — it would be scaling or upsampling.

✓ Correct. When a high-resolution image is displayed at a lower resolution, diagonal edges can appear jagged (aliased) as pixels become more visible. Anti-aliasing blends edge pixels with surrounding colours to create the visual impression of smooth lines.

mcQuestions.q: Which describes the result of lossy video compression?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Lossy compression permanently discards visual data to reduce file size. The removed data cannot be recovered, resulting in reduced image quality. The trade-off is a smaller file that is faster to transmit and store.
Lossless compression maintains the same quality but typically results in larger files than lossy formats. Lossy compression always involves a quality trade-off.
No change in quality would describe lossless compression — all original data is preserved. Lossy compression by definition changes the quality.
Compression cannot add quality beyond the original. Better quality with smaller size is physically impossible — reducing file size through lossy methods always involves discarding some data.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following is a 'serif' font?
optionExplanations: Arial is a sans-serif font — it has clean, straight letterforms with no decorative finishing strokes at the ends of characters.
Helvetica is one of the most famous sans-serif fonts, known for its clean, neutral design. It was the basis for Arial.
Calibri is a sans-serif font introduced by Microsoft. Its rounded, open letterforms are designed for on-screen readability.
✓ Correct. Times New Roman is a serif font — it has small decorative strokes (serifs) at the ends of letterforms, which help guide the reader's eye along lines of text in print.

mcQuestions.q: Scanners are typically used to
options: Convert an image into a digital file
optionExplanations: Converting numbers into files is a data processing or export function. Scanners capture visual information from physical documents — they don't process numerical data.
Converting text into animation is the function of animation software, not a scanner. Scanners capture static images.
✓ Correct. A scanner uses light sensors to capture the visual information on a physical document, photograph or object and converts it into a digital raster image file (JPEG, PNG, TIFF etc.).

Converting handwritten text into editable digital text requires OCR (Optical Character Recognition) software. A scanner alone only captures an image — it doesn't interpret or convert the text within it.

mcQuestions.q: What units are used to measure high speed video streaming?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Mbps (megabits per second) measures data transfer rate — how much data is transmitted each second. Video streaming quality is described in Mbps (e.g., Netflix HD requires 5 Mbps).
MHz (megahertz) measures the clock speed of a processor — how many cycles it performs per second. It is not used to measure data transfer rates.
MW stands for megawatts — a unit of electrical power. It has no relevance to data transmission or video streaming.
Tflops (teraflops) measures the computational performance of a processor — trillions of floating-point operations per second. It is used to compare GPU/CPU performance, not network speeds.

mcQuestions.q: What image type supports transparency?
optionExplanations: BMP (Bitmap) is an uncompressed raster format that does not support transparency. It always has a solid background.

✓ Correct. GIF supports transparency by allowing one colour in its 256-colour palette to be designated as transparent, making that colour invisible. PNG also supports transparency (with a full alpha channel).
JPEG does not support transparency. It uses lossy compression and always renders with a solid background — typically white or black where transparency would otherwise appear.
JPG and JPEG are the same format — different file extensions for identical data. Neither supports transparency for the same reason.

mcQuestions.q: Which technique can be used to digitally capture patterns of movement to animate a 3D character?
optionExplanations: Stop motion animates physical objects (puppets, clay models) by photographing them frame by frame with slight adjustments between shots. It does not digitally capture human movement.
Screen capture records what is displayed on a monitor. It is used for tutorials and software demonstrations — not for capturing physical movement to animate characters.

✓ Correct. Motion capture places sensors or optical markers on a real performer's body. Multiple cameras record the position of each marker in 3D space, and this movement data is applied to a digital 3D character to produce natural animation.
Motion graphics are animated design elements — text, shapes, icons — used in broadcast and titles. They are created in software, not by capturing real-world movement.

mcQuestions.q: Which technique is used to smooth jagged lines by blending the edge with pixels around it?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Anti-aliasing smooths the jagged staircase effect on diagonal edges by blending the colour of edge pixels with surrounding pixels, creating the visual impression of a smooth line.

Blurring softens the entire image or a selected area by averaging pixel colours across a wider area. While it can reduce sharpness of edges, it is not a targeted technique for smoothing aliased lines.
Morphing is an animation technique that smoothly transforms one image or shape into another over a sequence of frames. It has nothing to do with smoothing pixel edges.
Rendering is the process of generating a final 2D image from a 3D scene. Anti-aliasing may be applied during rendering, but rendering itself is not the smoothing technique.

mcQuestions.q: In what type of animation is tweening used?
optionExplanations: Cel-based animation involves drawing each frame by hand on transparent celluloid sheets. Tweening is the computer-automated alternative to this labour-intensive process.
'Still based' is not a standard animation type. Still images by definition have no movement to tween between.

✓ Correct. Tweening is used in path-based animation, where an object is assigned a path and keyframes define its position at specific points. The software automatically generates the in-between frames as the object travels along the path.
'Stop based' is not a recognised animation type. Stop motion animates by photographing objects frame by frame — tweening is not used in this process.

mcQuestions.q: Which type of file format is lossless?
optionExplanations: JPG (JPEG) uses lossy compression — it permanently discards image data to achieve smaller file sizes. The quality loss becomes more visible at higher compression levels.
MP3 uses lossy compression — it removes audio frequencies deemed less perceptible to the human ear, reducing file size but permanently discarding audio data.
MP4 is a container format that typically uses lossy video codecs (H.264, H.265). While it can contain lossless streams, it is not inherently lossless.
✓ Correct. PNG (Portable Network Graphics) uses lossless compression — all original pixel data is preserved exactly. The file can be fully decompressed and reconstructed without any loss of quality.

mcQuestions.q: Which frame rates should be used when producing slow-motion video?
optionExplanations: Recording and playing at the same low frame rate (12fps) produces normal speed video but with choppy, jerky motion — not slow motion.

✓ Correct. To produce slow motion, you record at a higher frame rate than you play back. Recording at 60fps then playing at 25fps means the footage plays at approximately 42% of real speed, creating smooth slow motion with plenty of frames to display.
Playing at 60fps but recording at only 25fps would create fast motion, not slow motion. The playback speed exceeds the recording speed, making footage appear accelerated.
Recording and playing at the same high frame rate (60fps) produces normal speed, smooth video — not slow motion. The frame rates must differ to achieve speed changes.

mcQuestions.q: How long (in seconds) to transfer 163,840 bytes at 10 megabits per second?
optionExplanations: 0.01 seconds would require transferring 163,840 bytes in 1/100th of a second — far faster than 10 Mbps can achieve. This is too small.
✓ Correct. Convert: 163,840 bytes × 8 = 1,310,720 bits ÷ 1,048,576 = 1.25 Mb. Time = 1.25 Mb ÷ 10 Mbps = 0.125 ≈ 0.13 seconds.
1.31 seconds is 10× too large — a common error from forgetting to convert bytes to bits (×8) before dividing by the transfer rate.
16.4 seconds would result from dividing bytes directly by Mbps without converting to bits first, confusing bytes and bits.

mcQuestions.q: A MIDI file contains
optionExplanations: MIDI files contain no audio recording whatsoever — they are instruction sets, not audio files. High-fidelity audio is stored in formats like WAV or FLAC.

✓ Correct. MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) stores music sequence data — instructions specifying which notes to play, at what pitch, velocity, duration and timing. A synthesiser or virtual instrument interprets these instructions to generate sound.
MIDI has nothing to do with video. It is a protocol for musical instruments and software to communicate note and timing data.
MIDI is not used for live streaming. It is a small, efficient instruction format used by musicians and composers — not a media streaming format.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following uses the process of motion capture?
options: Animating an object along a predefined path
Creating intermediate frames in an animation
Controlling the motion of an object automatically
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Motion capture records the physical movement of real people using sensors or optical markers. The captured data is then applied to 3D digital characters to produce natural, realistic animation.
Animating an object along a predefined path describes path-based animation, which uses keyframes and computer interpolation — not the physical capture of real movement.
Creating intermediate frames automatically describes tweening — a software process that generates frames between keyframes. It does not involve capturing physical movement.
Controlling motion automatically describes procedural or physics-based animation, where algorithms govern how objects move. This is generated mathematically, not captured from a person.

mcQuestions.q: What is the screen size in pixels for a full HD screen with 16:9 aspect ratio?
optionExplanations: 480 × 680 is not a standard resolution and does not represent a 16:9 ratio. This resembles SD (480p) dimensions but the numbers are incorrect.
1280 × 720 is HD (720p) at a 16:9 ratio — one step below Full HD. It offers less detail and is used for lower-quality streaming.
✓ Correct. Full HD (1080p) has a resolution of 1920 × 1080 pixels at a 16:9 aspect ratio. It is the standard for broadcast television, Blu-ray and most streaming services.
2560 × 1440 is QHD or 2K (1440p) — a higher resolution than Full HD, used in premium monitors and some smartphones. It is above Full HD, not Full HD itself.

mcQuestions.q: What does RTSP stand for?
optionExplanations: RTSP does not stand for 'server protocol'. The 'S' in RTSP stands for Streaming, and the 'P' stands for Protocol.
RTSP does not stand for 'server program'. A protocol and a program are fundamentally different things — a protocol is a set of communication rules, not software.
✓ Correct. RTSP stands for Real-Time Streaming Protocol — a network control protocol used to establish and control streaming media sessions, enabling functions like play, pause and seek.
RTSP is a protocol (a set of rules for communication), not a program (executable software). The distinction matters in networking and computing contexts.

mcQuestions.q: What is the function of progressive JPEG technology?
options: To make the image appear to load faster
optionExplanations: Progressive JPEG does not enhance colours. Colour adjustment is done through image editing tools like hue/saturation adjustments — not through the JPEG loading method.
Progressive JPEG does not increase resolution. The image resolution is fixed when the file is saved. Progressive loading only changes how the existing data is delivered to the browser.
Progressive JPEG does not achieve a smaller file size than baseline JPEG — they are typically similar in size. The difference is in the loading order, not the compression ratio.

✓ Correct. Progressive JPEG loads the entire image immediately at low quality, then progressively sharpens it in multiple passes. This gives users a visible preview of the whole image quickly, making the page feel faster to load compared to a baseline JPEG that loads line by line from top to bottom.

mcQuestions.q: What is the cause of poor quality audio with clipped waveforms?
options: Microphone too close to audio source
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Clipping occurs when the input recording level is set too high in the recording software or hardware interface. The incoming signal exceeds the maximum amplitude the system can capture, causing the tops and bottoms of the waveform to be 'clipped off', producing harsh, irreversible distortion.

Volume of input and recording level are related but distinct. It is specifically the recording/gain level setting in the interface or software that causes digital clipping — not just the loudness of the source.
A poor quality microphone produces poor frequency response, noise or low sensitivity — but not clipping. Clipping is a digital recording level problem, not a hardware quality issue.

A microphone too close to a loud source can cause acoustic overload (distortion in the microphone capsule), but digital clipping is specifically caused by the recording gain level being set too high, not physical proximity alone.

mcQuestions.q: Buffering is used when streaming video in order to
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Buffering preloads a portion of the video into memory ahead of the current playback position. This reserve of content ensures that minor fluctuations in internet speed don't immediately interrupt playback.
Loading content in real time with no buffer would mean any network interruption immediately pauses playback. Buffering exists precisely to prevent this by preloading ahead.
Buffering has nothing to do with interrupting an ISP connection — it is a client-side technique for managing variable network speeds smoothly.
Buffering does not cause slow connection speed. It is a response to variable connection speeds — a technique that hides network latency from the viewer.

mcQuestions.q: How does larger aperture affect an image recorded by a camera?
options: Allows a shallow depth of field
Increases sharpness of foreground and background
optionExplanations: A larger aperture decreases depth of field — the opposite of this option. Increased depth of field (more of the scene in focus) is achieved with a smaller aperture (higher f-number).

✓ Correct. A larger aperture (lower f-number, e.g., f/1.8) allows more light into the camera and creates a shallow depth of field — only a narrow plane is in sharp focus, while foreground and background appear blurred (bokeh effect).
A larger aperture allows more light into the camera, not less. Smaller apertures restrict light. This is a fundamental rule of exposure: larger aperture = more light.
Increasing sharpness of both foreground and background requires a small aperture (high f-number like f/16), which creates a wide depth of field — the opposite of a large aperture.

mcQuestions.q: How will an image be affected by color balance adjustments showing Cyan +4, Magenta -41, Yellow +15?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. In the CMY colour model, Magenta and Green are opposites — Magenta -41 is a large shift toward Green. Cyan and Red are opposites — Cyan +4 slightly reduces Red. Yellow +15 adds warmth. The dominant shift (Magenta -41) combined with Yellow +15 produces enhanced warm/red midtones.
Blue highlights would be enhanced by increasing Cyan and decreasing Yellow. Here, Yellow is increased (+15), which works against blue and shifts toward warmer tones.
Green midtones would be significantly enhanced if Magenta were reduced further, but the Yellow +15 counteracts this by shifting toward red/warm. The net result is red enhancement, not green.
Magenta highlights would be enhanced by increasing Magenta — but here Magenta is reduced (-41), which shifts the image away from Magenta, not toward it.

mcQuestions.q: Which image in the sequence uses stroke colour? (Image 1: outline star, Image 2: filled circle, Image 3: filled star)
optionExplanations: Image 1 is an outline-only star — it uses stroke colour for its outline with no fill. However, this option says 'only 1', which is incorrect because other images also use stroke colour.
Image 2 is a filled circle. It uses fill colour and also has a visible stroke/outline border. Saying 'only 2' is incorrect because image 3 also has a stroke.
Images 1 and 3 both have outlines, but image 1 has no fill (outline only) while images 2 and 3 have both fill and stroke. The question identifies which use stroke colour — both 2 and 3 do.

✓ Correct. Image 2 (filled circle) and Image 3 (filled star) both have a stroke colour applied to their outlines alongside fill colour. They display the combination of fill and stroke that distinguishes them from Image 1.

mcQuestions.q: Which is the best way to format headings and titles in a document?
options: Use any size and style desired
Apply same size and style as paragraph text
Make them larger in size and different in font style than body text
Style them slightly smaller with same style as paragraph text
optionExplanations: Using any size and style randomly creates an inconsistent, unprofessional document. Good design requires a systematic typographic hierarchy, not arbitrary choices.
If headings look identical to body text, they cannot be visually distinguished from the content they introduce. This eliminates the navigational purpose of a heading.

✓ Correct. Headings should be visually distinct from body text — larger in size and using a different weight or style (e.g., bold, different font) to create a clear visual hierarchy and guide readers through the document structure.
Making headings smaller than or the same size as body text defeats their purpose. Headings must be more visually prominent than the text they introduce to establish hierarchy.

mcQuestions.q: Which term describes the process where an animated image repeats indefinitely?
optionExplanations: Blending combines two images or layers together by mixing their pixels or adjusting transparency. It does not describe an animation playing repeatedly.
Keyframing sets specific frames that define the start and end states of a motion. It is part of the animation creation process, not a description of how an animation plays back.
✓ Correct. Looping is the process of playing an animation sequence continuously from start to finish and repeating it indefinitely. Animated GIFs and loading spinners commonly use looping.
Morphing is an animation technique that smoothly transforms one image or shape into a different image or shape over a sequence of frames. It describes a transformation, not repeated playback.

mcQuestions.q: What is object layering?
options: Preparing audio and video for editing
Combining visual elements from separate sources into single visual element
Preparing musical soundtrack using multiple sources
Combining audio and video from separate sources into single project file
optionExplanations: Preparing audio and video for editing describes pre-production or media organisation tasks, not object layering. Object layering is a visual compositing technique.

✓ Correct. Object layering stacks visual elements (images, graphics, shapes, text) from separate sources on independent layers to create a single composite visual. Each layer can be edited independently. This is fundamental to Photoshop, Illustrator and animation software.
Preparing a musical soundtrack from multiple sources describes audio mixing or music production, not object layering. Layering in audio is a separate concept from visual object layering.

Combining audio and video into a single project file describes video editing (e.g., in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve). Object layering specifically refers to stacking visual elements, not merging different media types.

mcQuestions.q: What term describes broadcasting and listening to on-demand music over the internet?
optionExplanations: Interactive describes content that responds to user input — not specifically the delivery method for on-demand music. While streaming services have interactive interfaces, 'interactive' doesn't describe the delivery technology.
Playback means playing back stored media on a local device. On-demand music over the internet is delivered in real time as it is received — not from a fully downloaded local file.

✓ Correct. Streaming delivers audio or video content over the internet in real time, playing the media as it is received rather than downloading it completely first. Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube all use streaming.

Transmitting is a general term for sending any data from one point to another. While streaming involves data transmission, 'transmitting' doesn't specifically describe the on-demand broadcasting of music content.

mcQuestions.q: Which process is used for smoothing edges by blending colours with adjacent colours?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Anti-aliasing smooths jagged diagonal edges in digital images by blending the colours of edge pixels with the pixels immediately surrounding them, creating the visual illusion of smooth curves and lines.
Posterising reduces the number of colours in an image to create a flat, graphic poster-like effect. It simplifies colour gradients — the opposite of blending edge pixels smoothly.
Object layering stacks visual elements on independent layers in image editing or animation software. It has no direct relationship to smoothing pixel edges.

File compression reduces the data size of a file. While lossy compression affects pixels, it is not a targeted process for smoothing edges — it affects the entire image's data, often introducing artefacts rather than smoothing edges.

mcQuestions.q: What is the primary purpose of video compression?
options: Reduce size of file and maintain quality
Minimise time taken for file to download
Convert video file to another format
Decrease size of file and reduce video quality
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. The primary purpose of video compression is to reduce file size while maintaining the best possible visual quality. Good codecs intelligently remove redundant or imperceptible data to achieve small files with minimal visible quality loss.

Minimising download time is a benefit that results from smaller file sizes, but it is not the primary purpose of compression itself. The goal is efficient storage and transmission, of which faster downloads are a consequence.
Converting a video file to a different format is transcoding — a separate operation. Compression may occur during transcoding, but format conversion is not what compression is primarily for.
Decreasing quality is a side effect of aggressive lossy compression, not the purpose. The goal is always to maintain as much quality as possible while achieving the target file size reduction.

mcQuestions.q: Which best describes 3D modelling for animation?
options: Visual illusion of depth of 3D objects
optionExplanations: A visual illusion of depth describes techniques like perspective, shading or stereoscopic viewing — these create the perception of depth in a 2D image. 3D modelling actually defines objects in three-dimensional space mathematically.

Mathematical transition describes how objects change position or shape over time — that is animation or transformation, not the model itself. A 3D model is a static mathematical description of a shape.

✓ Correct. 3D modelling creates a mathematical representation of a three-dimensional object using coordinates in X, Y and Z axes. The model is defined by vertices, edges and polygonal faces described mathematically, allowing rotation, scaling and animation.

A wireframe is a visual representation of a 3D model showing only its edges and vertices — it's a display mode used during modelling, not a definition of what 3D modelling is. The wireframe is a view of the mathematical model, not the model itself.

mcQuestions.q: Which best describes a font?
options: It has many sizes and styles
It is a design of type for a set of similar characters
It consists of a particular typeface in single sizing and style
optionExplanations: Having many sizes and styles describes a typeface family (e.g., Arial), which includes all its variations — Arial Regular, Arial Bold, Arial Italic in all sizes. A single font is just one of those variations.
A font family (or typeface family) contains related styles and weights. A font is a specific member of that family — not the family itself.

A design of type for a set of similar characters better describes a typeface — the overall visual design concept (e.g., Times New Roman as a design). A font is a specific implementation of that design at a specific size and style.

✓ Correct. A font is a specific instance of a typeface in a particular size and style — for example, 'Times New Roman Bold 12pt' is one font. The typeface (Times New Roman) is the broader design; the font is one specific variation.

mcQuestions.q: Which correctly describes a multimedia authoring tool?
options: Hardware used to display a multimedia title
Hardware used to capture multimedia elements
Software used for editing each multimedia element
Software used for creating complete multimedia title with interactivity
optionExplanations: A display device (monitor, projector, screen) is hardware — but it is used to output multimedia, not to create it. An authoring tool is software, not hardware.
Hardware used to capture multimedia elements describes input devices like cameras, microphones and scanners. These capture individual media elements — they are not authoring tools.

Software used for editing each element describes individual editing applications: Photoshop for images, Audacity for audio, Premiere for video. An authoring tool assembles all these elements together into a complete product.

✓ Correct. A multimedia authoring tool is software used to integrate and assemble all multimedia elements — text, images, audio, video, animation — into a complete, interactive multimedia product ready for distribution. Examples include Adobe Animate and Articulate Storyline.

mcQuestions.q: Which statement is true about using images from the internet?
options: Legal obligation to credit the author
Downloaded images can be used without permission if no profit made
Permission not required when using images without copyright notice
optionExplanations: Most internet images are protected by copyright automatically. 'Free to use' only applies to images under Creative Commons or Public Domain licences — which are the minority. Assuming images are free to use is a common and legally risky mistake.

✓ Correct. Many Creative Commons licences require attribution (crediting the author) as a legal condition of use. Even when images can be used, there is often a legal obligation to credit the original creator.
Making no profit does not grant permission to use copyrighted material. Copyright law protects creators regardless of whether the user profits financially from the use.
Copyright is automatic and does not require a copyright notice. The absence of a © symbol or watermark does not mean an image is free to use — it is still protected by law.

mcQuestions.q: When text on a page is fully justified, it is aligned
optionExplanations: Text aligned to the left only is called left-aligned or ragged right — the left edge is straight but the right edge is uneven. This is not full justification.
Text aligned only to the right is right-aligned — the right edge is straight but the left is ragged. This is not full justification.
Text aligned to the centre has both edges uneven, with each line centred in the column. This is centred alignment, not full justification.

✓ Correct. Full justification aligns text to both the left and right margins simultaneously by adjusting word spacing so each line fills the full column width. This creates neat, uniform edges on both sides, commonly seen in newspapers and books.

mcQuestions.q: Which file format supports transparent backgrounds?
optionExplanations: BMP (Bitmap) is an uncompressed raster format developed by Microsoft. It does not support transparency — it always renders with a solid background.
JPEG uses lossy compression optimised for photographs. It does not support transparency — areas that would be transparent appear as solid white or black depending on the application.

✓ Correct. PNG (Portable Network Graphics) supports transparency through an alpha channel, which controls the opacity of individual pixels from fully transparent to fully opaque. This allows PNG images to overlay seamlessly on any background.
RAW is an unprocessed sensor data format used by cameras. It is designed for maximum quality and editing flexibility in post-production — it does not support transparency as a display format.

mcQuestions.q: A web-based survey uses a drop-down list to
options: Guide the user to the correct answer
Limit the possible answers a user can enter
Limit the number of characters a user can enter
Guide the web designer to include correct answers
optionExplanations: A drop-down list presents options without indicating which one is 'correct' — surveys don't have right answers in that sense. The list standardises responses, not guides users to a predetermined correct answer.

✓ Correct. A drop-down list presents users with a predefined set of choices, limiting their input to only those options. This ensures data consistency and validity by preventing free-text responses that might be inconsistent, misspelled or outside the expected range.
Limiting the number of characters is the function of a text input field with a maxlength attribute, or a character counter widget. Drop-down lists don't limit characters — they limit choices.
Drop-down lists are for users completing the survey, not for the web designer. The designer creates the list options beforehand; the list then constrains what respondents can select.

mcQuestions.q: What characterises 'motion capture' as an animation technique?
options: Tracking human movements to animate digital characters
Using mathematical formulas for movement manipulation
optionExplanations: Drawing individual frames by hand describes traditional hand-drawn (cel) animation. Motion capture replaces this process with recorded real-world movement data applied to digital characters.

Using transparent sheets (celluloid) for animation describes classic cel animation — the technique used before digital animation. Motion capture is a digital recording technique with no physical sheets involved.

✓ Correct. Motion capture tracks the real-world movements of human performers using sensors, cameras or optical markers. This movement data is recorded and applied to 3D digital characters to produce natural, realistic animation that reflects actual human movement.

Using mathematical formulas for movement describes procedural animation — where algorithms define how objects move based on rules. Motion capture uses recorded real movement data, not mathematical formulas.

mcQuestions.q: Which encoding technique maintains original quality while reducing file size?
optionExplanations: Encryption scrambles data to secure it from unauthorised access — it is a security technique, not a compression method. Encrypted files are typically larger than unencrypted ones due to added overhead.
Decompression is the process of restoring compressed data to its original form. It expands file size — it is the reverse of compression, not a way to reduce file size.
Lossy compression reduces file size by permanently discarding data. While it achieves greater size reductions, it does not maintain original quality — some data is irreversibly lost.

✓ Correct. Lossless compression reduces file size by encoding data more efficiently without discarding any information. The original file can be perfectly reconstructed from the compressed version. Examples include PNG for images and FLAC for audio.

mcQuestions.q: What is the standard video size for full HD video?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Full HD (1080p) has a resolution of 1920 × 1080 pixels at a 16:9 aspect ratio. It is the broadcasting standard for television, streaming services like Netflix and most consumer display devices.
2048 × 1080 is the DCI 2K resolution standard used in digital cinema projection — slightly wider than Full HD but not the consumer Full HD standard.
3840 × 2160 is 4K Ultra HD (UHD) — four times the pixel count of Full HD. It offers significantly more detail but requires more bandwidth and storage than Full HD.
7680 × 4320 is 8K UHD — sixteen times the pixel count of Full HD. It is an emerging consumer format with very limited content availability and extremely high storage requirements.

mcQuestions.q: What does the 'hue' adjustment tool primarily affect?
options: Lightness or darkness of the image
Colours that are present in the image
optionExplanations: Sharpness is adjusted using dedicated sharpening tools (Unsharp Mask, Smart Sharpen) that increase edge contrast. Hue has no effect on how sharp or blurry an image appears.
Colour intensity (the vividness or saturation of colours) is controlled by the Saturation slider. Hue shifts which colours are present, not how vivid they are.
Lightness or darkness is controlled by Brightness, Exposure or Luminance adjustments. Hue adjustment does not affect how light or dark the image is.

✓ Correct. Hue refers to the actual colour (red, blue, green, yellow etc.) in the colour model. Adjusting hue rotates all colours around the colour wheel — for example, making reds shift toward orange, or greens toward cyan.

mcQuestions.q: What advantage does progressive loading of web pages offer?
options: Images can be re-sent if interrupted
A web page can partially load as being viewed
It sends entire image as one complete file
A blank page displays until all content ready
optionExplanations: Resending interrupted files describes error-correction protocols (like TCP) that handle dropped packets. Progressive loading is about the order in which content renders, not about error recovery.

✓ Correct. Progressive loading allows a web page to display and become usable as content loads incrementally. Users can read text and interact with the page while remaining images and scripts continue loading in the background, significantly improving perceived performance.
Sending an entire image as one complete file before displaying it describes baseline (non-progressive) loading — this would result in a blank space until the image is fully received.

A blank page that waits until all content is ready describes the old baseline loading behaviour that progressive loading was designed to improve upon. Progressive loading shows partial content, not a blank page.

mcQuestions.q: Which statement correctly describes storage of analogue video?
options: Analogue video is stored in binary code
Analogue video is stored on magnetic tape
Both analogue and digital share same storage format
Analogue video stored in discrete, non-continuous magnetic tape
optionExplanations: Binary code (0s and 1s) is how digital data is stored. Analogue video is a continuously varying signal — it does not use binary encoding. Binary storage is a defining characteristic of digital, not analogue, media.

✓ Correct. Analogue video is stored as a continuously varying magnetic signal on magnetic tape (e.g., VHS, Betamax, U-matic). The signal is a direct analogue — a continuous physical representation — of the original light and sound waves.

Analogue and digital storage are fundamentally different. Digital video uses binary encoding on solid-state, optical or magnetic media. Analogue video uses continuous magnetic variation on tape. They are not interchangeable formats.

Analogue signals are continuous and non-discrete — the variation is smooth and uninterrupted, not made up of separate discrete steps. Discrete, non-continuous storage is a characteristic of digital data, not analogue.

mcQuestions.q: Which stage of animation typically involves the use of wire frames?
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Wireframes are used during previsualisation (previs) — the planning stage of 3D production where rough skeletal models of characters and environments are created to plan camera angles, movement and timing before detailed modelling begins.

Post-production handles editing, colour grading, sound design and visual effects compositing after principal photography or animation is complete. By this stage, wireframes have long been replaced by fully textured and rendered assets.
Storyboarding uses 2D sketches or illustrations to plan the visual sequence of shots and camera angles. It is a 2D planning tool, not a 3D wireframe technique.

Rendering is the final stage that converts the fully modelled, textured and lit 3D scene into finished 2D images or video frames. Wireframes are replaced by complete models well before the rendering stage.

mcQuestions.q: What is the primary purpose of paragraph formatting in a word processing document?
options: To ensure documents have a unique appearance
To add special effects like animations and transitions
To make documents easier to read and visually appealing
To aid in creating complex layouts with images and tables
optionExplanations: Making a document unique is a design goal, but not the primary purpose of paragraph formatting. Paragraph formatting focuses on readability and visual organisation — consistency and clarity, not uniqueness.

Animations and transitions are features of presentation software (e.g. PowerPoint), not paragraph formatting in word processing. Paragraph formatting deals with spacing, indents, alignment and line height.

✓ Correct. The primary purpose of paragraph formatting is to make documents easier to read and visually appealing — through controlling line spacing, indentation, alignment and paragraph spacing to create clear, readable structure.

Complex layouts with images and tables are created using page layout, columns and table tools, not paragraph formatting. Paragraph formatting specifically controls the appearance of text blocks within the document.

mcQuestions.q: What is the primary advantage of using dedicated screenshot tools over keyboard shortcuts?
options: They are faster and more efficient.
They offer a visual interface for selecting capture areas and settings.
They are more readily available on a wide variety of operating systems.
optionExplanations: Keyboard shortcuts (e.g. Print Screen, Cmd+Shift+4) are often faster for quick captures since they require no additional software to open. Dedicated tools are not necessarily faster.
Screenshot tools have no effect on computer processing speeds. Processing speed is determined by CPU, RAM and the running software — not by which screenshot method is used.

✓ Correct. Dedicated screenshot tools (e.g. Snipping Tool, Lightshot, Greenshot) offer a visual interface that allows users to precisely select the capture area, annotate images, set timers, choose output formats and access settings — providing far more control than basic keyboard shortcuts.

Keyboard shortcuts for screenshots are built into virtually every major operating system (Windows, macOS, Linux). Dedicated tools typically require separate installation, making them less universally available, not more.

mcQuestions.q: Which factor most commonly affects sound quality when streaming audio on the World Wide Web?
options: The popularity of the audio file
The type of speakers used by the listener
The compression methods applied to reduce file size
optionExplanations: Popularity of an audio file does not affect its audio quality. A widely streamed file is identical in quality to a rarely played one — popularity affects server load, not audio fidelity.
The original recording location affects the acoustic environment captured, but once a file is digitised and uploaded, the recording location has no further impact on streamed audio quality.

The type of speakers affects how audio is reproduced at the listener's end, but does not change the quality of the audio file itself. Poor speakers cannot improve a low-quality file, but excellent speakers cannot fix compression artefacts either.

✓ Correct. The compression method applied to an audio file most commonly affects its streaming quality. Lossy compression (e.g. MP3 at low bit rates) discards audio data to reduce file size, introducing artefacts and reducing fidelity. Higher compression ratios result in smaller files but noticeably poorer audio quality.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the effect of using a contrast filter in multimedia design?
options: The transitions between colours are smoothed out.
A uniform colour tone is applied across the entire image.
The brightness levels are adjusted without altering the colour balance.
The difference between the light and dark areas of an image is increased.
optionExplanations: Smoothing transitions between colours describes blending or gradient tools. A contrast filter does the opposite — it increases the difference between tones rather than smoothing them.
Applying a uniform colour tone describes colour overlay, tint or colour balance adjustments. Contrast adjustment affects the tonal range of light and dark, not the colour hue across the image.

Adjusting brightness without altering colour balance describes a brightness adjustment, not contrast. Contrast specifically changes the ratio between highlights and shadows, not just overall brightness.

✓ Correct. A contrast filter increases the difference between the lightest and darkest areas of an image — making light areas lighter and dark areas darker. High contrast produces vivid, dramatic images; low contrast produces flatter, softer tones.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following post-editing techniques is commonly used to create slow-motion effects in video?
options: Using software to generate additional frames between existing frames
Increasing the frame rate of the original footage during playback
Applying a digital filter to reduce the video resolution
Reversing the playback direction of the footage
optionExplanations: ✓ Correct. Software-based frame interpolation (e.g. optical flow in Adobe Premiere, DaVinci Resolve) generates additional intermediate frames between existing frames, allowing footage shot at a normal frame rate to be played back more slowly without motion becoming choppy. This is a common post-production slow-motion technique.

Increasing the frame rate during playback would actually make footage appear faster, not slower. To create slow motion in playback, you need the source footage recorded at a higher frame rate than the playback rate — or you generate extra frames in post.
Reducing video resolution affects image quality and file size but has no effect on playback speed or the slow-motion effect. Resolution and frame rate are independent properties.
Reversing playback direction creates a rewind or reverse effect — it plays footage backwards, not slower. This is a different creative technique unrelated to slow motion.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of rigging in 3D animation?
options: Modelling characters and objects in a scene
Setting up a skeleton structure for character movement
Creating realistic backgrounds and environments in a scene
Creating detailed textures and lighting effects for the final render
optionExplanations: Modelling is the process of creating the 3D geometry (shape and form) of characters and objects. This happens before rigging — you must model the character before you can rig it for animation.

✓ Correct. Rigging is the process of setting up a hierarchical skeleton structure (armature) inside a 3D character model. This skeleton system controls how the model deforms and moves when animated — allowing animators to pose and animate the character naturally.

Creating backgrounds and environments is part of 3D scene design and environment modelling. It is a separate process from rigging, which specifically involves the internal skeleton and control structure of a character.
Creating textures and lighting effects is part of shading, texturing and lighting — processes that happen after rigging and animation are complete, during the look development and rendering stages.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following is most important for video player software to play videos smoothly?
options: High screen brightness for better visibility
A high-quality sound card for clearer audio
A faster processor to handle video playback
Extra storage space to keep more video files
optionExplanations: Screen brightness is a display setting controlled by the monitor or screen — it affects visibility but has no bearing on whether the software can decode and display video frames smoothly.
A sound card handles audio output quality. While important for audio fidelity, it does not affect the video player's ability to decode and render video frames at the required frame rate.

✓ Correct. A faster processor (CPU) — or dedicated GPU with hardware decoding — is most important for smooth video playback. The processor must decode compressed video data (e.g. H.264, H.265) and render frames fast enough to maintain the required frame rate. Insufficient processing power causes stuttering and dropped frames.
Storage space determines how many files can be stored but does not affect playback smoothness. Playback performance depends on processing power and memory (RAM), not available storage capacity.

mcQuestions.q: What is a key limitation of PDF files that hinders collaboration and editing?
options: Dependence on proprietary software limits accessibility.
They are difficult to modify without specialised software.
They are unable to embed fonts, images and other multimedia elements.
They lack security features, making them unsuitable for sharing sensitive information.
optionExplanations: PDF files can be opened with free software (Adobe Acrobat Reader, web browsers, Preview on macOS) on virtually any device. Accessibility is actually a strength of PDFs, not a limitation.

✓ Correct. PDFs are designed primarily as fixed-layout presentation documents rather than editable files. Modifying PDF content — changing text, restructuring layouts, editing images — requires specialised software (e.g. Adobe Acrobat Pro) that is often costly. This makes collaborative editing and iterative revisions significantly more difficult than with native formats like Word or Google Docs.
PDFs can embed fonts, high-resolution images, vector graphics, hyperlinks, form fields and multimedia elements. The inability to embed content is not a limitation of the PDF format.

PDFs actually have strong security features — including password protection, encryption, digital signatures and restrictions on printing/copying. Security is a recognised strength of the format, not a limitation.

mcQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes animation as a multimedia element?
options: A special effect used to enhance the appearance of static images
A method of displaying still images to convey a single idea or message
A process where images are displayed in quick succession to simulate movement
A technique that combines visual and audio elements to create an immersive experience
optionExplanations: Special effects enhance or transform images but are not the definition of animation. Effects like filters, colour grading or overlays can be applied to static images without any animation being involved.
Displaying still images to convey a single idea describes a photograph or illustration. Animation specifically involves displaying a sequence of images in rapid succession — not a single still image.

✓ Correct. Animation is defined as the process of displaying a series of images (frames) in quick succession to create the illusion of movement. The human eye and brain perceive the rapid sequence as continuous motion — this is the fundamental principle of all animation, from cel animation to CGI.

Combining visual and audio elements to create an immersive experience describes multimedia more broadly, or specifically describes audiovisual production. Animation does not require an audio element — it is defined by the illusion of movement created by sequential images.

mcQuestions.q: A website wants to implement an age verification system to restrict access to adult content. Which of the following methods would be the most reliable for ensuring accurate age control?
options: Using facial recognition software to estimate age
Sending a verification code to the user's email address
Requiring users to upload a government-issued ID for verification
Using CAPTCHA tests to ensure the user is human before age verification
optionExplanations: Facial recognition can estimate approximate age but is unreliable for precise age verification — it can be fooled by photos, has significant accuracy limitations, and raises serious privacy concerns regarding biometric data collection.

Sending a verification code to an email address confirms access to that email account but does not verify the user's age. Anyone — including minors — can create an email account without age verification.

✓ Correct. Requiring users to upload a government-issued ID (passport, driver's licence) is the most reliable age verification method because it uses an authoritative, independently verified document. The ID contains the user's date of birth and can be cross-checked against government records or third-party verification services.
CAPTCHA tests verify that the user is human (not a bot) but provide absolutely no information about the user's age. A CAPTCHA can be solved by anyone regardless of their age.

writtenQuestions.q: What does RTSP stand for?
writtenQuestions.answer: Real Time Streaming Protocol

writtenQuestions.q: Outline how motion capture technology works.
writtenQuestions.answer: Optical motion capture systems use reflective markers placed on key points of an actor's body (joints, limbs, face). Multiple infrared cameras track the position of each marker in 3D space simultaneously. The captured positional data is transmitted to a computer, which assembles it into a skeleton model that approximates the character's movements in real time. This data is then mapped onto a digital 3D character model during post-production, producing natural, realistic animation that would be extremely difficult to achieve by hand.

bandDescriptors.full: 2/2 — Explains that optical markers are placed on a performer's body, tracked by multiple infrared cameras in 3D space, and the positional data is used to animate a digital character model.
bandDescriptors.partial: 1/2 — Mentions markers and cameras or refers to capturing movement data, but the link to animating a digital character is missing or vague.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/2 — Describes motion capture only as 'recording movement' with no explanation of how it works technically.

writtenQuestions.q: A client requires a print run of 15,000 pages. Paper $25.00 per ream (500 sheets), Black toner $45.00 per cartridge (2000 pages capacity), Colour toner $65.00 per cartridge (650 pages capacity). Calculate the total cost.

bandDescriptors.full: 3/3 — Correct method applied for all three cost components (paper: 30 reams × $25 = $750; black toner: 8 cartridges × $45 = $360; colour toner: 24 cartridges × $65 = $1,560) with rounding up applied where needed, arriving at total of $2,670. Working shown.
bandDescriptors.partial: 1–2/3 — Correct method for most components but one arithmetic error or one rounding error (e.g. 7.5 cartridges not rounded up to 8) leads to an incorrect total.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/3 — Incorrect method for two or more components, or answer only with no working shown.

writtenQuestions.q: Describe how large MP4 files can be reduced in size when authoring for DVD media.
writtenQuestions.answer: Large MP4 files can be reduced in size through several techniques. First, reducing the bit rate forces less data to be stored per second of video, directly decreasing file size, though some quality loss may result. Second, lowering the video resolution (e.g., from 1920×1080 to 1280×720) reduces the number of pixels per frame, significantly cutting file size. Third, reducing the frame rate (e.g., from 60fps to 25fps) means fewer frames are stored per second. Fourth, trimming unwanted sections of the video using editing software removes unnecessary data. Finally, converting to a more efficient codec (such as H.265/HEVC instead of H.264) can achieve smaller file sizes at the same visual quality, making the file more suitable for DVD authoring.

bandDescriptors.full: 4/4 — Describes at least four distinct techniques: reducing bit rate (less data per second), lowering resolution (fewer pixels per frame), reducing frame rate (fewer frames per second), trimming unnecessary footage, and/or converting to a more efficient codec (e.g. H.265). Acknowledges the quality trade-off.
bandDescriptors.partial: 2–3/4 — Describes two or three techniques with reasonable explanation. May repeat the same idea differently rather than identifying genuinely distinct methods.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1/4 — Identifies at most one technique without explaining the mechanism by which it actually reduces file size.

writtenQuestions.q: Describe the features that should be included on a company's website homepage.
writtenQuestions.answer: A company's homepage should include the following key features to be effective. A clear, prominent logo and company name immediately identify the brand and build trust. A concise headline or tagline communicates the company's purpose to visitors within seconds. Complete contact details — including address, phone number and email — make the business accessible. Navigation links (including a site map) allow users to easily locate all services and return to the homepage at any point. High-quality photos or graphics illustrating the company's products or services create visual appeal and convey professionalism. A search function enables visitors to quickly locate specific information. Social proof elements such as client testimonials, reviews or awards build credibility. Calls to action (e.g., "Contact us", "Get a quote") guide users toward desired outcomes. Special offers or subscription options encourage user engagement and return visits.

bandDescriptors.full: 5/5 — Identifies and explains at least five distinct homepage features — e.g. logo/branding, headline/tagline, contact details, navigation links/site map, quality imagery, search function, calls to action, testimonials. Explains the purpose of each feature, not just listing it.
bandDescriptors.partial: 3–4/5 — Identifies multiple features but explanations are brief or some features are listed without explaining why they matter.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1–2/5 — Names one or two features only, with no explanation of the purpose each feature serves on the homepage.

writtenQuestions.q: Which software is best suited to creating vector graphics?
writtenQuestions.answer: Adobe Illustrator (or Corel Draw, Inkscape, Affinity Designer — any dedicated vector-based drawing application).

writtenQuestions.q: Calculate the file size in megabytes (MB) of a 1920 x 1080 pixel image with a bit depth of 32. Include all working.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Step 1 — Total pixels: 1920 × 1080 = 2,073,600 pixels
Step 2 — Total bits: 2,073,600 × 32 bits = 66,355,200 bits
Step 3 — Convert to bytes: 66,355,200 ÷ 8 = 8,294,400 bytes
Step 4 — Convert to MB: 8,294,400 ÷ 1,048,576 (1024²) = 7.91 MB

bandDescriptors.full: 3/3 — All four steps shown with correct values: total pixels (1920 × 1080 = 2,073,600), total bits (× 32 = 66,355,200), bytes (÷ 8 = 8,294,400), megabytes (÷ 1,048,576 = 7.91 MB). Final answer 7.91 MB (or 7.9 MB accepted).
bandDescriptors.partial: 1–2/3 — Correct method applied but one conversion step is wrong (e.g. dividing by 1,000,000 instead of 1,048,576 for MB). Working shown.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/3 — Incorrect method, missing steps, or answer given with no working.

writtenQuestions.q: Explain the effects of video compression on image quality and data storage.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Video compression reduces file size to make video more practical to store, share and stream. There are two main types with contrasting effects on quality and storage.

Lossy compression (e.g., MP4/H.264) achieves significant file size reduction by permanently discarding visual data the human eye is least likely to notice — such as repeating background pixels and subtle colour variations. This results in smaller files that require less storage space, but at the cost of reduced image quality, which becomes more visible at higher compression ratios.

Lossless compression (e.g., RAW video, ProRes) preserves all original image data, maintaining full quality. However, this results in very large file sizes that demand significantly more storage capacity and processing power, making them impractical for consumer distribution.

High-end video cameras that shoot in raw lossless formats produce extremely large files that typically require post-processing before distribution. Most streaming platforms and consumer devices use lossy codecs, which use algorithms to remove redundant data (such as unchanged pixels between frames) to balance quality against manageable file sizes.

bandDescriptors.full: 4/4 — Distinguishes between lossy (e.g. MP4/H.264 — permanently discards data, smaller files, quality loss at high compression ratios) and lossless compression (e.g. ProRes/RAW — preserves all original data, full quality, very large files). Addresses BOTH image quality AND data storage effects for each type.
bandDescriptors.partial: 2–3/4 — Discusses compression effects on file size or quality but does not clearly distinguish lossy from lossless, or only addresses one of the two required impacts (quality OR storage, not both).
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1/4 — Vague description of 'compression makes files smaller but reduces quality' without explaining how or distinguishing compression types.

writtenQuestions.q: Explain ethical issues that need to be considered in the development and use of multimedia products.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The development and use of multimedia products raises several important ethical and legal issues that creators and users must consider.

Copyright and intellectual property are the most significant concerns. Multimedia designers must obtain appropriate licensing for all third-party software, images, audio and video used in their products. Using copyrighted material without permission or payment constitutes infringement and can result in legal action. This protects the intellectual property rights of original creators and ensures they are fairly compensated for their work.

Classification and audience appropriateness is another key issue. When producing multimedia content for public distribution or sale, creators must ensure it carries an appropriate Australian Classification (e.g., G, PG, M, MA15+) so consumers can make informed decisions about its suitability for their audience, particularly children.

Privacy must also be considered when using images, audio recordings or video footage of individuals. Consent must be obtained before using anyone's likeness in a commercial or publicly distributed product.

Finally, consumers themselves have ethical obligations. Illegally copying, sharing or distributing copyrighted multimedia content — even for personal use — violates Australian copyright law and undermines the creative industry. Adhering to fair use guidelines and purchasing legitimate licences are both ethical and legal requirements.

bandDescriptors.full: 5/5 — Identifies and explains at least three distinct ethical/legal issues: copyright and licensing (obtaining permission and payment for third-party content), content classification (G/PG/M/MA15+ ratings for audience appropriateness), privacy and consent (using individuals' likenesses), and/or consumer obligations (illegal copying, fair use). Explains both the issue and why it matters.
bandDescriptors.partial: 3–4/5 — Identifies two or three issues correctly but the explanation of the consequences or obligations is incomplete for one or more. May focus heavily on copyright alone.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1–2/5 — Mentions copyright only in general terms, or lists issues without explaining what the specific obligation or legal consequence actually is.

writtenQuestions.q: Identify an advantage of using PDF files.
writtenQuestions.answer: PDF files maintain consistent formatting across different operating systems, devices and software applications. They can also be password-protected to prevent unauthorised editing.

bandDescriptors.full: 1/1 — States a valid, specific advantage — e.g. PDF maintains consistent formatting across different devices and operating systems, or PDFs can be password-protected to prevent unauthorised editing.
bandDescriptors.partial: 0/1 — Too vague to award the mark (e.g. 'they are easy to use') or states an advantage that applies equally to most other file types.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/1 — Incorrect or irrelevant advantage stated.

writtenQuestions.q: Outline the purpose of an online thumbnail.
writtenQuestions.answer: A thumbnail is a small, reduced-resolution copy of a larger image or video. Its primary purpose on a web page is to reduce download time and bandwidth usage, since loading a small preview is far faster than loading the full-resolution file. Thumbnails also allow users to visually browse and preview content — such as images in a gallery or videos in a playlist — without needing to download the full file, improving the user experience and navigation efficiency.

bandDescriptors.full: 2/2 — Explains that thumbnails are small preview images that (1) reduce download time and bandwidth usage, AND (2) allow users to visually browse and preview content without loading the full file.
bandDescriptors.partial: 1/2 — States only one purpose (e.g. 'they load faster') without explaining the browsing/preview function, or vice versa.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/2 — Response does not identify thumbnails as small preview images, or does not explain their purpose in reducing download time and enabling content browsing.

writtenQuestions.q: Calculate the time required (in seconds) to transfer a 550 MB file at 80 megabits per second. Include all working.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Step 1 — Convert megabytes to megabits: 550 MB × 8 = 4,400 megabits
Step 2 — Divide by transfer rate: 4,400 Mb ÷ 80 Mbps = 55 seconds

bandDescriptors.full: 3/3 — Correctly converts 550 MB to megabits (× 8 = 4,400 Mb) then divides by 80 Mbps to arrive at 55 seconds. Both steps shown with working.
bandDescriptors.partial: 1–2/3 — Method correct but arithmetic error leads to wrong final answer. Or correct answer of 55 seconds without showing the MB-to-Mb conversion step.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/3 — No conversion from MB to Mb attempted, or incorrect formula used entirely.

writtenQuestions.q: Describe an advantage and a disadvantage of virtual reality.
writtenQuestions.answer:
Advantage: Virtual reality enables users to safely experience dangerous, expensive or impossible scenarios in a fully immersive simulated environment. This has significant benefits for training purposes — for example, military personnel, surgeons, pilots and emergency responders can rehearse high-risk situations without any real-world danger or cost. The interactive, first-person experience also creates high levels of engagement and information retention compared to traditional training methods.

Disadvantage: Virtual reality requires expensive specialist hardware (headsets, motion controllers, high-performance computers) and sophisticated software, making it costly to implement and maintain, particularly at scale. Additionally, some users experience adverse physical effects such as motion sickness, eye strain or disorientation after extended use, which limits the duration and accessibility of VR experiences.

bandDescriptors.full: 4/4 — Clearly explains ONE substantial advantage (e.g. safe training for dangerous scenarios, immersive/interactive learning, cost-effective simulation) AND ONE substantial disadvantage (e.g. expensive specialist hardware, motion sickness or eye strain, limited accessibility on lower-end devices). Both explained with reasoning.
bandDescriptors.partial: 2–3/4 — Identifies both an advantage and disadvantage but the explanation of one is superficial or the example is not developed.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1/4 — States only an advantage or only a disadvantage, or both stated with no explanation of why they are significant.

writtenQuestions.q: An animator has drawn various mouth shapes for a character. Explain how the animator can use the mouth shapes to produce quality dialogue in the animation.
writtenQuestions.answer:
The animator can use the pre-drawn mouth shapes as a reference library of assets called phonemes — visual representations of different speech sounds. To produce quality dialogue, the animator first imports the audio dialogue track into the animation software and places it on the timeline. They then analyse the waveform to identify which sounds occur at which frames.

Each mouth shape is matched to its corresponding phoneme at the correct point on the timeline, ensuring the character's mouth movements align precisely with the spoken audio — a process called lip-syncing or synchronisation. Techniques such as tweening are used between mouth shapes to generate smooth transition frames automatically, avoiding jerky or unnatural movement. Morphing can also be applied to blend between shapes fluidly.

The animator then plays back the sequence to check that the mouth movements feel natural and are precisely synchronised with the audio track, making adjustments to timing as necessary. This approach ensures the final dialogue appears convincing and professional, significantly improving the perceived quality of the animation.

bandDescriptors.full: 5/5 — Explains that mouth shapes (phonemes) are matched to the audio waveform on the timeline (lip-syncing). Mentions tweening to generate smooth in-between frames and morphing to blend between shapes fluently. Describes the playback/review process to verify synchronisation.
bandDescriptors.partial: 3–4/5 — Explains the general lip-sync process and mentions the timeline but omits tweening/morphing techniques, or does not describe waveform analysis or the review step.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 1–2/5 — Describes matching mouths to words generally without any technical terminology (tweening, morphing, waveform, timeline, phoneme).

writtenQuestions.q: Identify a key characteristic of fully immersive virtual reality.
writtenQuestions.answer: Interactivity — the user can actively engage with and manipulate the virtual environment. Also acceptable: sensory feedback (visual, auditory, haptic) or believability (the sense of presence within the virtual world).

writtenQuestions.q: Outline ONE disadvantage of using high-resolution graphics when creating a multimedia product.
writtenQuestions.answer: A significant disadvantage of using high-resolution graphics in a multimedia product is that they substantially increase file size. Larger files require more storage space and take longer to load, which can result in poor user experience — particularly for web-based products where slow load times may cause users to abandon the content. High-resolution graphics also demand greater processing power to render and display, which can cause performance issues or lag on lower-end devices, limiting the product's accessibility.

bandDescriptors.full: 2/2 — Identifies increased file size as the disadvantage AND explains at least one consequence: slower loading times for web users, more storage space required, or greater processing demands causing performance issues on lower-end devices.
bandDescriptors.partial: 1/2 — States 'large file size' without explaining why this is a problem in context, or mentions slow loading without linking it to file size.
bandDescriptors.minimal: 0/2 — Neither a valid advantage nor a valid disadvantage of VR is identified, or both are too vague to award any marks.

writtenQuestions.q: Calculate the cost of producing 800 double-sided business cards with gloss finish on one side and custom design. Price per unit: $0.85 for 500-999 double-sided, Gloss: $0.10, Custom design: $60.

Gloss finish: 800 × $0.10 = $80.00
Custom design: $60.00 (flat fee)
